_purpose: Shared source registry. Claims cite source_ids rather than restating a citation, so a source's assessment is corrected in one place and every claim depending on it re-derives.
_rules: Every entry is a real document that was actually retrieved or returned by search on the accessed_on date.
No entry may be created from model knowledge. If a source could not be reached, that is recorded in retrieval_note rather than the citation being written from memory.
source_type follows the Phase 3C-2 priority: official_government > primary_source > official_business > reputable_secondary.

sources.title: NRS 116.3102 — Powers of unit-owners' association; limitations
sources.publisher: Nevada Revised Statutes (via nv.elaws.us statutory mirror)
supports_claims: An association may cause a vehicle to be removed when it is improperly parked 'on property owned or leased by the association' or 'on any road, street, alley or other thoroughfare within the common-interest community in violation of the governing documents'.

Written or oral notice must be given at least 48 hours before the association may direct removal, except where the vehicle blocks a fire hydrant, fire lane or accessible parking space, or poses an imminent threat to health, safety or welfare.
sources.notes_limitations: Statutory mirror, not the Legislature's own server — leg.state.nv.us returned HTTP 403 to automated retrieval, as did law.justia.com. Text is corroborated by the Nevada Real Estate Division training material (source red-cic-towing-fastref) and by Justia search results. The retrieved extract did NOT state who bears the towing cost; that specific point remains unconfirmed here.

sources.title: Fast Reference — Towing, NRS 116.3102 Powers of unit-owners' association
sources.publisher: Nevada Real Estate Division, Department of Business and Industry
supports_claims: Association removal power is exercised over vehicles improperly parked on roads, streets, alleys or other thoroughfares within the common-interest community.
48-hour notice must be posted conspicuously on the vehicle or given to its owner or operator before the association may direct removal.
Costs incurred for towing and storage are borne by the owner of the vehicle.
sources.notes_limitations: Direct PDF retrieval was rejected by the host ('Request Rejected'). Content is from the search index of this official document, not the retrieved file. Treated as corroborating rather than primary until someone opens the PDF directly. The towing-cost point rests on this source alone.
sources.retrieval_note: Direct fetch blocked 2026-09-05; content obtained via web search of the official URL.

sources.title: NRS 116.31031 — Power of executive board to impose fines and other sanctions for violations of governing documents
sources.publisher: Justia (reproducing Nevada Revised Statutes, 2025 code year)
supports_claims: Where the violation does not pose an imminent threat to health, safety or welfare, a fine must not exceed $100 for each violation, or $1,000 in total per hearing against a unit's owner or tenant.
The homeowner must be given notice and a reasonable opportunity to be heard before a fine is imposed.

A violation not cured within 14 days (or a longer period set by the executive board) is deemed a continuing violation, after which an additional fine may be imposed for each 7-day period the violation remains uncured.
sources.notes_limitations: Justia reproduces statutory text but is a secondary publisher. Direct retrieval of both leg.state.nv.us and Justia returned HTTP 403; this content came via the search index. The 7-day continuing-fine period is the load-bearing detail here and should be confirmed against the Legislature's own text before publication.
sources.retrieval_note: Direct fetch blocked 2026-09-05; content obtained via web search.

sources.title: Vehicle Title and Ownership / Application for Duplicate Nevada Certificate of Title (VP-012)
supports_claims: Form VP-012 is the Application for Duplicate Nevada Certificate of Title.
The title fee is $20.00 when the vehicle remains in Nevada, and $35.00 where the vehicle is not physically located or registered in Nevada.
A Title Processing Fee of $8.25 is charged on all title transactions, making the in-state duplicate total $28.25.
sources.notes_limitations: Content obtained via search of the official DMV pages (dmv.nv.gov/title.htm and dmv.nv.gov/pdfforms/vp012.pdf). Fee schedules change; this requires re-checking before any published use.
sources.retrieval_note: Obtained via web search restricted to dmv.nv.gov, 2026-09-05.

sources.title: NRS Chapter 487 — Repair, Removal and Disposal of Vehicles
supports_claims: Chapter 487 governs automobile wreckers, salvage titles and the disposal of wrecked, salvage, nonrepairable, abandoned and junk vehicles.
A licence is required to dismantle, scrap, process or wreck a vehicle.
sources.notes_limitations: SEARCHED AND NOT FOUND: no provision was located in NRS 487, NRS 482 or the DMV salvage pages permitting the sale of a junk vehicle without a title on the basis of model year (e.g. 'model year 2010 or older'). Absence of evidence after a targeted search is recorded here so the claim is not re-argued from memory later. This is not proof no such provision exists — it is proof it was not found.
sources.retrieval_note: Search restricted to leg.state.nv.us, dmv.nv.gov and nv.gov, 2026-09-05.

sources.title: Clark County Code Title 11 — Abatement of Nuisances
supports_claims: Clark County Code Title 11 governs abatement of nuisances in UNINCORPORATED Clark County.
Inoperative vehicles stored on private property are treated as a nuisance violation in unincorporated Clark County, enforced by the county's Code Enforcement / Public Response Office.
sources.notes_limitations: Obtained via search of Municode and clarkcountynv.gov; the specific section text and timelines were not retrieved. Applies only to unincorporated areas — incorporated cities have their own codes.
sources.retrieval_note: Search restricted to clarkcountynv.gov and municode, 2026-09-05.

sources.title: Henderson Municipal Code Chapter 7.08 — Nuisance; Office of Public Response (Code Enforcement)
supports_claims: The City of Henderson enforces nuisance and property-maintenance rules under its own municipal code, separately from Clark County.
Abandoned, inoperable and junk vehicles are among the violations Henderson's Office of Public Response enforces.
sources.notes_limitations: Obtained via search of Municode and cityofhenderson.com. Section text, notice periods and penalties were NOT retrieved and remain unverified.
sources.retrieval_note: Search restricted to cityofhenderson.com and municode, 2026-09-05.
